title: Chat boundary sanitizer + tokenizer probing in onboarding pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We onboard new open models weekly. During onboarding we publish a performance profile and pin a default model version. We frequently observe small but user-visible regressions caused by differences in tokenizer behavior and chat template delimiters across model variants (role markers, invisible prefix tokens, newline/space handling). These lead to token budgeting mismatches and degraded latency/cost estimates for customers who pin versions.

Problem statement:
1) Onboarded performance profiles sometimes misestimate token counts because our pipeline assumes a canonical tokenization.
2) Chat templates rendered by customers may map to different token sequences across model variants, causing inconsistent rollouts when customers pin versions.
3) There's no automated gating for tokenizer-template compatibility; issues surface post-release.

Proposed solution:
- Add a "chat-boundary sanitizer" stage to the onboarding pipeline that canonicalizes common delimiters (role headers, separator tokens) into a tolerant intermediate form before token counting and prefix/KV cache estimation. The sanitizer emits both canonical and normalized templates for auditing.
- Implement a "tokenizer probing" routine that runs a set of representative prompt permutations (role orders, edge-case delimiters, long prefix scenarios) against the tokenizer for each model variant and records: tokenized length, first-token ids, and presence of invisible prefix tokens.
- Use probing outputs to compute a small compatibility report attached to the model's onboarding artifact and to adjust the published token budget and latency/cost estimates in the performance profile. If divergence exceeds thresholds, set onboarding status to "manual review required".
- Persist a lightweight mapping heuristics file per model (human-readable, reversible) that runtime can use to normalize incoming chat messages when customers opt into "compatibility normalization".

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline produces a compatibility report for every new model onboarding run with pass/fail flag.
- For 95% of curated prompt permutations, the sanitized token count estimate is within +/- 2 tokens of the real tokenized length on the model.
- Models with >5% prompt permutations failing threshold are marked for manual review and do not auto-publish performance profile.
- Performance profile published includes a field "tokenizer_compatibility" with status and probe-summary link.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype sanitizer as a small Go binary invoked in onboarding container. Keep deterministic transforms and a flag to run in dry-run only. (Owner: Liam)
2) Build tokenizer-probing harness in onboarding runner (Python) that loads model tokenizer and runs test matrix. (Owner: Priya Singh - contractor).
3) Add compatibility report storage in onboarding artifacts bucket (S3 key with model-id + probe-v1).
4) Wire gating logic: onboarding platform will check report and only push performance profile if pass.
5) Add runtime flag and small adapter to Console to surface the compatibility report link.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sanitizer may over-normalize and hide model-specific behaviors. Mitigation: keep operations reversible and include original examples in report.
- Risk: Probing adds latency to onboarding runs. Mitigation: parallelize probes and run in best-effort mode for non-critical channels; enforce gating only for hosted models.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for sanitizer transforms and round-trip property.
- Integration test running end-to-end onboarding with a known set of models (include two with known edge tokenizer behaviors).
- Smoke test: upload a customer chat template and verify runtime normalization yields same token count as onboarding estimate.

Metrics to monitor post-release:
- Fraction of onboards flagged for manual review due to tokenizer mismatch (target < 2%).
- Variance between estimated vs actual token usage in first 24h of live traffic (target mean error < 1.5 tokens).
- Time added to onboarding runs (target < 20% overhead).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: deploy sanitizer in dry-run mode and collect compatibility reports across new onboards.
- Week 2: enable gating for small set of models; surface reports in Console.
- Week 3: enable compatibility-normalization adapter as opt-in runtime feature for enterprise customers.

Notes and links:
- Proto PR for tokenizer probing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/244
- Design doc: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/onboarding-tokenizer-probe
